quotes.text: Unless you’re maintaining an existing Billing Meters integration, use [Metronome](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/usage-based.md) — Stripe’s primary usage-based billing platform — for any new integration, including adding usage-based pricing to existing flat-rate subscriptions.
Basic usage-based billing supports billing credits that reconcile at invoice time, but customers can exceed their balance during the cycle.
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.

Billing credits only apply to [subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/object.md#invoice_object-subscription) line items that link to a [meter price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md#price_object-recurring-meter). The [Usage Records API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/usage_records.md) isn’t supported.
If you represent your customers as customer-configured [Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md), pass the `Account` ID to the `customer` parameter.

old_evidence.text: If your integration uses [customer-configured Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/create.md#v2_create_accounts-configuration-customer), replace `Customer` and event references in the code examples with the equivalent Accounts v2 API references.
With this version of usage-based billing, credits are burned down when the invoice is created at the end of the billing period.
(Optional) Under **Eligibility**, specify a list of usage-based prices that this credit grant applies to.

findings: New lines 9-24 add explicit Stripe recommendation of Metronome for new usage-based integrations and compare basic Billing Meters with Metronome. This is a product-selection change absent from the May capture; it is guidance within this November snapshot, not proof of Billing Meters deprecation, forced migration, or account eligibility. The existing concept already states the broad recommendation, but this source page does not.

New lines 177-215 replace the prior generic Accounts v2 substitution note at old line 187 with explicit availability and preview-version qualifications, customer-configured Account creation, and separate Accounts v2/Customers v1 examples. New lines 244-269, 297-315, 394-441, and 456-493 show customer_account versus customer for credit grant, subscription, balance, transaction, and funding routes. Preserve the identities and preview scope.

New line 504 adds a specific Account ID instruction for the event-summary customer parameter, even though the example at lines 510-515 uses CUSTOMER_ID. New meter-event example at lines 336-342 also uses CUSTOMER_ID. Avoid silently rewriting either example to imply every customer identifier parameter has the same shape.

The guide still limits credit grants to metered-price subscription line items, not Usage Records (new line 226; old line 219); burn at invoice creation/end of billing period remains (new line 224; old line 217), while applicable credits are applied after invoice finalization (new line 375; old line 371). The deleted preview sign-up email does not establish a changed preview status.

The source page at lines 19 and 42 calls credits indiscriminate across all meters yet itself notes optional price Eligibility, matching new line 239 and old line 232. A source update should avoid an unconditional all-meter guarantee and distinguish the guide's broad example from optional grant scoping.
substantive_changes: Added Metronome recommendation and feature comparison for new integrations; basic Billing Meters path remains explicitly documented for existing integrations (new lines 9-24).

Added explicit Accounts v2 versus Customers v1 API routes and availability/preview qualifications, including customer_account parameters on several billing resources (new lines 177-215, 244-269, 297-315, 394-441, 456-493).
Added Account ID guidance for the event-summary customer parameter (new line 504).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May guide used Node SDK examples including Decimal.from('3') and Decimal.from('5') for price requests (old lines 139-150 and 171-182); November curl numeric form values do not prove Node SDK removal or a general Decimal.from requirement.

The guide's basic Billing Meters credit timing and limitations remain: invoice-time burn, metered-price subscription items only, no Usage Records API support, possible in-cycle overspend, and async meter summaries/upcoming invoices (old lines 215-219, 355, 371, 486; new lines 18, 224-226, 363, 375, 508).
The old guide already mentioned customer-configured Accounts as an alternative (old line 187), although November makes concrete route differences and availability qualifications explicit.
Optional grant eligibility by price and priority remain available (old lines 231-232; new lines 238-239), despite broad introductory wording about credits across meters.
conflicts: New Metronome comparison says basic usage-based billing customers and teams 'can’t see live credit balances or usage totals mid-cycle' at line 17, yet the same guide provides available balance lookup at lines 383-412 and custom-period meter summaries at lines 502-508. Interpret the comparison as lack of real-time reconciliation, not absence of any mid-cycle query.

Both versions say credits apply indiscriminately across meters (new line 28; old line 10), while both offer optional usage-based price eligibility (new line 239; old line 232). The source's unconditional all-meter wording at lines 19 and 42 should be narrowed.

The new guide recommends customer-configured Accounts for most use cases at line 183 but its meter-event example still passes CUSTOMER_ID at line 340, and its event-summary prose says Account ID goes into customer while the curl example uses CUSTOMER_ID at lines 504 and 513. This is example/prose identity ambiguity, not grounds to infer a tested Account-based meter-event payload.
unresolved_questions: The captures do not establish whether a specific non-Connect Stripe account has Accounts v2 preview access; the new guide says public preview and names a preview header for such users (new lines 179-181, 193-206).

The new guide does not show an Accounts v2-specific meter-event payload example or explain whether CUSTOMER_ID placeholders at lines 340 and 513 should be replaced by an Account ID; no account operation was performed.

New Accounts v2 funding examples show invoice and invoice-item creation but only the Customers v1 section shows a finalize request (new lines 456-500). Treat this as an incomplete Accounts v2 example, not proof finalization differs.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/use-cases/credits-based-pricing-model, [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-credits]] now needs to reflect the November guide's recommendation to use Metronome for new usage-based integrations, while retaining basic Billing Meters for existing integrations (new lines 9-24; old lines 4-10 lacked that section). The capture also introduces qualified Accounts v2 and Customers v1 paths (new lines 177-215, 244-269), replacing the older generic Account substitution note (old line 187); the curl versus Node change alone is a rendering/example change.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/use-cases/credits-based-pricing-model, [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-credits]] warrants source_required_update because the current source at lines 13-59 lacks the new product recommendation and scoped customer identity routes. Preserve invoice-time burn and metered-price-only eligibility, supported by old lines 215-219 and new lines 222-226; clarify that optional price eligibility exists in both snapshots (old line 232; new line 239). Do not infer Billing Meters deprecation, universal Accounts v2 availability, or real-time basic credit balance from the November text.
